metadata.description: Comprehensive information for visualizing horses in 2D and 3D art, animation, and design

basic_measurements.name: Head as unit of measure
basic_measurements.description: Horse's head length is often used as baseline measurement unit
basic_measurements.standard_proportions: A typical adult horse is approximately 2.5 heads tall at the withers and 3 heads long from chest to rump
basic_measurements.anatomical_note: The head-to-body ratio varies by breed, with Arabians typically having smaller heads relative to body size than draft breeds

basic_measurements.name: Height to length ratio
basic_measurements.description: Ratio of height at withers to body length (point of shoulder to point of buttock)

standards.square_horse: Equal height and length, common in Arabians
standards.rectangular_horse: Longer than tall, common in Thoroughbreds and many sport horses

basic_measurements.measurement_tips: Body length is measured from point of shoulder (not front of chest) to point of buttock (not end of rump)

basic_measurements.name: Topline measurements
basic_measurements.description: Proportional relationships of the back segments

standards.withers_to_croup: Should be approximately 1/3 of total body length
standards.loin_length: Ideally short and strong, approximately 1/6 of total body length

basic_measurements.name: Balance point
basic_measurements.description: The visual center of gravity in the horse
basic_measurements.location: Typically falls at the girth area, just behind the elbow
basic_measurements.visualization_importance: Essential for depicting weight distribution and believable poses
basic_measurements.shifting_factors: Changes with head position, collection, and movement

line_art.description: Techniques for capturing horse form using outlines and contours
key_points: Focus on flowing lines to capture movement
Pay special attention to joining points (shoulder, hip, neck/head)
Emphasize characteristic curves (topline, underline, facial profile)

construction_methods.name: Geometric blocking
construction_methods.description: Using basic shapes to establish proportions before adding detail
steps: Establish center of balance with oval for barrel
Add circles for major joint positions
Connect with straight lines for limbs
Refine with curves following muscle and bone structure

construction_methods.name: Gesture drawing
construction_methods.description: Capturing the energy and motion with minimal lines
steps: Start with action line showing spine curve
Add directional lines for neck, limbs
construction_methods.benefits: Creates more dynamic, lively horses even in static poses

techniques.name: Cross-hatching
